entities.summary: Saint Vulmar was a French priest, hermit and then abbot who was later venerated as a saint. Born in Burgundy, France around 640, Vulmar turned to religion after his wife was taken from him and given to the man to whom she had previously been betrothed. This pivotal event marked the beginning of a lifelong devotion to his faith, which would eventually lead to his canonization. Vulmar's dedication to his spiritual calling was further solidified during his time as a hermit, where he spent years in solitude, praying and reflecting on his faith. His ascension to the position of abbot at the monastery of Saint-Pierre in Soissons, France, marked a significant turning point in his life, as he was now tasked with leading a community of monks and guiding them on their spiritual journeys. Vulmar's leadership and spiritual guidance played a significant role in the development of the Benedictine Order, which would go on to shape the spiritual landscape of Europe for centuries to come. As a result of his tireless efforts, Vulmar was eventually recognized as a saint by the Catholic Church, and his feast day is still celebrated by many Christians around the world today. In the years following his death in 697, Vulmar's legacy continued to grow, as his writings and teachings were widely disseminated throughout Europe, inspiring countless individuals to follow in his footsteps. Through his remarkable life and ministry, Vulmar serves as a powerful reminder of the enduring power of faith and the importance of living a life of service to others.
